short: A stepped temple tower of ancient Mesopotamia.
note: An ancient Mesopotamian temple tower built in receding stages, with a shrine at its summit.

short: Latin: “What I have written.”
note: The opening of Quod scripsi, scripsi: “What I have written, I have written.” In John 19:22, Pontius Pilate refuses to change the inscription placed above the crucified Jesus.

short: A brand name for rigid polystyrene foam.
note: A trademark for extruded polystyrene foam. The name is also used loosely for other lightweight foamed-polystyrene products.

sources.label: DuPont: Styrofoam is not a cup

short: A boat with two parallel hulls.
note: A vessel with two hulls joined side by side; the word comes through Tamil from a term for tied logs.

short: A short, heavy wool coat, often plaid.
note: A coat made from thick woolen cloth, commonly with a plaid pattern; also the name of the fabric itself.

short: The distinctive quality of a voice or musical tone.
note: The quality that makes one voice or instrument sound different from another, even at the same pitch and loudness.

short: An earthy yellow or reddish-brown color.
note: An iron-bearing earth used as yellow, brown, or red pigment, and the color of that pigment. Also spelled ochre.

short: A heavy hammer or splitting tool.
note: A large, heavy-headed hammer; a splitting maul has a wedge-shaped head for splitting wood.

short: The cartoon bear of Jellystone Park.
note: The cartoon bear known for taking picnic baskets in Jellystone Park, accompanied by Boo Boo and pursued by Ranger Smith.

sources.label: Warner Bros. and National Wildlife Federation: Yogi Bear activity guide

short: Ford’s sport-utility vehicle, introduced in 1966.
note: A Ford vehicle line introduced in 1966 as a compact four-wheel-drive vehicle for use on and off roads.

short: The American luxury-car marque.
note: The car company founded by Henry Leland and named for Abraham Lincoln. It became part of Ford in 1922.

sources.label: Ford: Edsel Ford and the Lincoln DNA

short: A small, brimless hat with a flat crown.
note: A round hat with upright sides and a flat top, named for its resemblance to a small box for pills.

short: A slim, rigid case for carrying papers.
note: A small, usually rectangular case for business papers. Attaché is French for an official attached to a diplomatic mission.

short: A British slang intensifier: extremely or vigorously.
note: Billy-o intensifies an expression, especially in “like billy-o,” meaning very hard, fast, or strongly. Its origin is uncertain.

short: Possibly Culver Military Academy in Indiana.
note: Possibly Culver Military Academy, a boys’ boarding school in Culver, Indiana, founded in 1894.

short: Fretful or inclined to complain.
note: Habitually complaining, or expressing complaint in an irritable, whining manner.

short: Relating to the fluid-filled sac surrounding a developing embryo.
note: The amnion is the thin membrane enclosing an embryo or fetus; amniotic fluid fills the protective sac around it.

short: The ancient Mesopotamian city in present-day Iraq.
note: A major city on the Euphrates in ancient Mesopotamia, in present-day Iraq. Its religious monuments included Etemenanki, a great ziggurat.

short: American actor, singer, dancer, and comedian.
note: Danny Kaye (1911–1987), born David Daniel Kaminsky, was an American entertainer known for physical comedy, rapid verbal routines, and musical performances.

sources.label: Library of Congress: Danny Kaye onstage
Library of Congress: Danny Kaye and Sylvia Fine collection

short: An American brand of vegetable cooking oil.
note: An American brand of vegetable cooking oils, sold for frying, baking, and other kitchen uses.

short: A brand of waterproof adhesive medical tape.
note: Wet-Pruf is a trade name for waterproof, oil-resistant adhesive tape. Curity is a related medical-dressing and tape brand.

sources.label: Kendall medical catalog: Wet-Pruf and Curity tapes

short: The legendary musician who led away Hamelin’s children.
note: The Pied Piper of Hamelin removes a town’s rats with his music; after the townspeople withhold his payment, he leads their children away. Robert Browning retold the legend in his 1842 poem.

sources.label: Robert Browning: The Pied Piper of Hamelin

short: The international hotel chain.
note: Ramada is a hotel brand whose roadside inns became familiar across the United States and later internationally.

short: Household spirits in folklore; also a division of Girl Scouts.
note: In Scottish and northern British folklore, brownies are small household spirits that perform chores, often in return for food left for them. Brownies is also the name for a younger age division of Girl Scouts and Girl Guides.

sources.label: Thomas Keightley: The Fairy Mythology, “The Brownie”

short: The preparation of animal skins as lifelike specimens.
note: The practice of preserving an animal’s skin and mounting it on a supporting form so that it resembles the living animal.

short: An American underwear brand.
note: An American underwear brand historically associated with the Duofold Health Underwear Company of Frankfort, New York.

short: The opening of Chaucer’s Canterbury Tales.
note: Geoffrey Chaucer’s General Prologue to The Canterbury Tales begins with April’s sweet showers piercing the drought of March down to the roots. The lines are in Middle English.

sources.label: Geoffrey Chaucer: The Canterbury Tales, General Prologue

short: Tomb-like, hollow, or funereal.
note: Relating to a tomb or burial; figuratively, gloomy or suggestive of death. A sepulchral voice is hollow and solemn.

short: A Finnish firearms manufacturer.
note: A Finnish maker of rifles, established in 1921.

short: Otherworldly or uncanny; formerly, fated to die.
note: Fey can mean uncanny or otherworldly. In older Scottish usage it describes someone doomed to die, or showing the strange behavior thought to precede death.

short: Heat transferred by electromagnetic waves.
note: Thermal radiation carries energy as electromagnetic waves and does not require air or other matter between the source and its surroundings.

sources.label: NASA Cosmicopia: Heat transfer in space

short: Heat carried by the movement of a fluid.
note: Heat transfer through the bulk movement of a liquid or gas, such as warm air rising and cooler air taking its place.

sources.label: NASA: Building Your First SINDA Model, review of basic heat transfer

short: Heat transferred through material contact.
note: Heat transfer through direct interactions within matter, or between materials that touch, without requiring the material as a whole to move.

sources.label: NASA: Building Your First SINDA Model, review of basic heat transfer

short: Small, pale spirits of Senegalese folklore.
note: Also spelled Yumboes: small, pale supernatural beings in Wolof folklore, recorded in Thomas Keightley’s The Fairy Mythology. They inhabit underground dwellings in hills near Gorée and take food from human settlements.

short: The lock brand founded by the Yale family.
note: A lock brand associated with Linus Yale and his son Linus Yale Jr., whose nineteenth-century inventions helped establish the modern pin-tumbler cylinder lock.

short: The public university in West Lafayette, Indiana.
note: Purdue University is a public research university in West Lafayette, Indiana, particularly associated with engineering, science, and aviation.

short: The U.S. National Aeronautics and Space Administration.
note: The United States’ civilian agency for aeronautics research, space science, and space exploration.

short: The biblical daughter of King David.
note: Tamar, daughter of King David and sister of Absalom, appears in 2 Samuel 13. Solomon, David’s son by Bathsheba, was her half-brother.

short: The biblical king celebrated for wisdom and wealth.
note: The son of David and Bathsheba who ruled Israel and built the Jerusalem Temple. The books of Kings emphasize his wisdom, riches, and trade, including gold brought from Ophir.

short: Possibly H. Rider Haggard’s lost-mine adventure.
note: Possibly H. Rider Haggard’s 1885 novel King Solomon’s Mines, in which travelers seek a lost African diamond mine associated with the biblical king.

sources.label: H. Rider Haggard: King Solomon’s Mines

short: The northeastern African region around the Somali peninsula.
note: A region commonly comprising Somalia, Ethiopia, Eritrea, and Djibouti, beside the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden, and Indian Ocean.

sources.label: IGAD: Countries of the Horn of Africa

short: The Yemeni port city on the Gulf of Aden.
note: A historic port in southern Yemen, built around a volcanic crater and long connected with Indian Ocean and Red Sea trade.

short: The country at the southwestern end of the Arabian Peninsula.
note: A country on the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, opposite the Horn of Africa; Aden is one of its principal historic ports.

short: The cotton-swab brand.
note: A brand name for small sticks tipped with cotton, commonly used more broadly for cotton swabs.

short: A light, silvery metal that burns with a brilliant white light.
note: The chemical element Mg, atomic number 12. Its low density makes magnesium alloys useful in lightweight structures, while its bright combustion made it useful in photographic flash equipment.

short: The British national anthem under a queen.
note: The national anthem otherwise known as God Save the King. Its words change with the reigning monarch; its tune was publicly performed in London in 1745.

sources.label: The Royal Family: The national anthem

short: Abraham Lincoln’s portrait on the U.S. cent.
note: The portrait of Abraham Lincoln, the sixteenth U.S. president, has appeared on the one-cent coin since 1909.

short: The astronomer who placed Earth among the planets orbiting the Sun.
note: Nicolaus Copernicus (1473–1543) developed the heliocentric model in which Earth rotates and travels around the Sun. His major account, De revolutionibus, was published in 1543.
